thread:
anjali: FYI brought up HF checkpoint on staging (hf/mistral-spm-1). conversion script ran but outputs look shifted. example: <pad> ended up at id 3 instead of 0.
kevin: ugh. Did the script run the SPM->BPE remap step or the fallback remapping? which tool/version?
anjali: using tooling in infra/ml/convert v0.9.2 (the one that uses sentencepiece->merge-table). command: `python tools/convert_hf.py --model hf/mistral-spm-1 --out redwood/mistral-bpe`
maria: can you paste the head of the vocab.json and the spm.vocab? sometimes SPM extra pieces like \u2581 or trailing-sentinel produce duplicate merges.
anjali: pasted below. note the special tokens block and the top 7 ids.
```
# from hf tokenizer.json (post-convert)
{"<pad>":3, "<s>":1, "</s>":2, "▁the":25, "▁to":32, "▁a":40}
```
```
# from the generated merges/bpe_vocab
0:"<s>"
1:"</s>"
2:"▁unk"
3:"<pad>"
4:"▁"
...
```
kevin: that ordering suggests the convert step appended SPM reserved tokens at the end, then wrote a new special tokens mapping with different offsets. convert-bot might have applied a `reserve_specials=True` fallback.
ryan: also check config.json model_max_length and tokenizer_class fields. HF SentencePieceTokenizer sometimes sets `special_tokens_map` differently and the converter assumes BPE-style reserved id ordering (pad=0). mismatch causes id-shift upstream.
anjali: interesting — quant eval shows weird regression on L4 syntactic tests after quantize-int8. could the id shift be silently changing logits for token 0 during kv-cache restore?
maria: yes. If pad/cls/sentinel ids move, the KV caching alignment can produce off-by-one contexts; generation can then pick wrong continuation tokens.
kevin: repro steps I'd try: 1) run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(tokenizer.get_vocab().get('<pad>'))"` on HF export 2) run the redwood-converter with `--emit-vocab-mapping` 3) diff the mapping and run a small prompt through both tokenizers to compare token ids.
anjali: did that, here's quick diff output (trimmed):
```
# hf ids
'<pad>':0
'<s>':1
'</s>':2
# redwood post-convert
'<s>':0
'</s>':1
'▁':2
'<pad>':3
```
ryan: that's the cause. convert tool assumed SPM had no explicit pad token and slid everything. Two fixes: A) preserve HF special token ids when present (prefer), B) rewrite model weights/token mappings to match new ids (riskier).
maria: also saw a `chat_template` mapping failure in console — templates expect `<|system|>` at id 0. because we changed ordering, the chat routing used wrong role token.
anjali: for now I rolled back the conversion on staging and attached the failed conversion artifacts to the ticket. can we add a guard in converter that fails if special token set/order differs from expected? like: 
```
if set(hf_specials) != set(converted_specials):
    raise RuntimeError('special token mismatch: abort conversion')
```
kevin: agreed. we should also add a `--preserve-special-ids` flag that maps BPE output into the HF original id slots (even if it creates holes in the vocab). that will make quant experiments deterministic.
convert-bot: automated note: created issue ML-4821 with logs and attached `vocab_diff.txt`.
anjali: next steps for me: try `--preserve-special-ids` patch, re-run conversion, run small quant-int8 smoke tests, and a 100-sample eval across our eval set. I'll post results. @kevin @maria any other quick checks?
maria: check merge-table stability: if sentencepiece uses suffix-only pieces the merge ordering can flip when you collapse pieces into BPE merges. add an assert that vocab_size_post_convert == declared_vocab_size in config.json.
kevin: and include a tiny script to validate chattemplate token usage: ensure tokens referenced by templates map to same ids after conversion.
anjali: perfect. I'll iterate today and push a PR to repo/infra/ml/convert with the guard + preserve flag. will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
ryan: thanks — ping me if you want a dedicated staging slot for re-run (might need GPU time).
anjali: will do, gracias.
